requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Compare recognizable site context with site-overhead.png and boundary geometry, north and scale with site-plan.png. The plan must include a north arrow and scale bar consistent with the supplied existing-site plan. Drawing style and abstraction may vary, but relocation, mirroring or replacement of the real surroundings fails. The supplied aerial defines existing appearance; proposed park work may change the interior as commissioned.

The plan must show an unbroken walking circuit, a concentrated tree grove and an identifiable open lawn. The section must describe the same loop with a 1.5 m clear width and proposed 1% crossfall. Route shape may vary within the site; disconnected path fragments or conflicting loop specifications fail.

Read the zoning and material records together. The four allocations must total 4,882 m² with paths included rather than added as a fifth area. Grove Walk and Quiet Garden use compacted crushed stone; Play Commons combines broom-finished concrete with its permeable area; Open Lawn combines grass with a compacted crushed-stone path. Shade must correspond to a dense grove, canopies and shelters, canopies, and edge canopies respectively. Zone shapes may vary; missing zones, changed allocations or incompatible surface assignments fail.

Require three visibly distinct spatial proposals led by a dense grove, built shelters and connected activity clearings respectively, each contained within the existing A–D boundary. Presentation styles may vary; renamed copies of one layout or expansion outside the boundary fail.

The record must select one offered direction and give three reasons addressing shade, through-walking and the relationship of N2 to N3. All written schedules must develop that selection, with stated stage order or cross-references establishing selection first. The presentation opening page must name the same choice. File timestamps alone do not establish sequence; ambiguous choice, missing reasons or inconsistent development fails.

The masterplan must explicitly identify the recorded direction and retain its defining landscape organization. Developed detail may change; a conflicting identification or replacement of the selected organizing approach fails.

Each image must legibly print the project name and phrase, all four exact zone-name/area pairs and AR—Acer rubrum, QR—Quercus rubra, CO—Celtis occidentalis, CS—Cornus sericea and CP—Carex pensylvanica. Compare with the written schedules and fixed client facts. Entry order may vary; missing entries, spelling changes, incorrect codes or changed areas fail.

Every target must state the four exact zone-name/area pairs. The plant schedule and presentation must also contain the five correct botanical-name/code pairs, MAPLE COURT and Room for every day. The two-page site analysis must include the five botanical names and schedule capacities of 30, 40, 20 and 35, together with each zone's principal surface and shade method from the fact sheet. Page arrangement may vary; missing required records or conflicting mappings fail.

Require AB 64.1 m, BC 76.3 m, CD 64.2 m and DA 75.9 m on the correct boundary edges and a site area of approximately 4,882 m². Existing trees and retained features must remain at recorded positions. Map lighting and N1 caregiver seating in Grove Walk, N2 shared activity in Play Commons, N3 quiet seating in Quiet Garden and N4 gentle exercise at the Open Lawn edge. Capacities must match the site analysis in zone order. Graphic conventions may vary; omitted, moved or contradictory records fail.

Both documents must associate Phase 1 with Grove Walk and Quiet Garden totaling 2,482 m², and Phase 2 with Play Commons and Open Lawn totaling 2,400 m². The implementation schedule must assign N1 and N3 with associated paths, planting, seating and lighting to Phase 1, and N2 and N4 with associated paths, planting, shelters, permeable concrete and lighting to Phase 2. Formatting may vary; swapped zones, incorrect totals or missing scheduled scope fails.

Compare the plan, planting sheet and early schedule for matching grove and lawn positions, three planting layers, plant totals and the Play Commons permeable area. Distinct mapped canopy and shelter footprints must cover 720 m² and 180 m² of walking and sitting surfaces without double counting. The sheet schedule must repeat six each of AR, QR and CO at 60 mm trunk caliper, 36 CS at 600 mm height and 240 CP at 90 mm pot diameter, plus the specified paving construction. Diagram styles may vary; conflicting locations, counts, sizes or construction fail.

Read both schedules for six AR, six QR and six CO, each at 60 mm trunk caliper; 36 CS at 600 mm height; and 240 CP at 90 mm pot diameter. Require a compacted crushed-stone loop with 1.5 m clear width and 1% crossfall, 120 m² of 120 mm permeable concrete over 200 mm open-graded aggregate at N2, and broom-finished concrete elsewhere in Play Commons. Materials must include timber seating slats on galvanized steel frames, steel planting edges and timber slat shelter canopies on galvanized steel posts. Equivalent tabular presentation is allowed; substituted specifications or incomplete entries fail.

Both images must explicitly dimension the clear loop width, transverse slope, resulting fall and concrete and aggregate thicknesses. The section must show concrete above aggregate and correspond to the mapped N2 paving and loop. Annotation placement may vary; absent values, reversed layers or conflicting details fail.

The separation section must cut through the actual N2–N3 planted buffer and dimension its width at no less than 8 m. The lawn section and N4 node plan must depict the same lawn boundary and adjoining loop relationship as the masterplan, with readable relevant dimensions. Section orientation may vary; unrelated cuts, insufficient planting width or displaced lawn/path relationships fail.

Each sheet must contain a node plan, readable dimensions relevant to seating or activity and a perspective of its assigned use and masterplan location. N1 must demonstrate caregiver seating with a view toward N2; N3 must support quiet sitting and N4 gentle exercise at the lawn edge. Detail and viewpoint may vary; missing representations, swapped activities or inconsistent node geometry fail.

Compare each node's pair separately. Each must identify summer 12:00 and 21:00 states while retaining camera position, orientation, framing and fixed trees, paving, shelters and furniture. Different nodes may use different cameras. Each node must match its developed plan and activity, with nighttime fixtures consistent with mapped lighting. People and illumination may change; a moved camera within a pair or altered fixed design fails.

Review the entire 10-second sequence for travel along the masterplan loop through N1, N2, N3 and N4, daytime use and evening views of both N2 and N3. Spatial relationships, node furniture, planting and paving must correspond to the developed drawings and scenes. Camera movement and editing may vary; a skipped node, inconsistent route, missing evening location or changed node design fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Require at least twelve pages and recognizable reuse of every listed source, including all three sections, all four node designs and both implementation phases. Written schedules may be reformatted and drawings may be resized or cropped while preserving relevant information. Omitted sources, illegible reuse or replacement with contradictory work fails.

The presentation must visibly include identifiable reuse of at least one supplied summer daytime scene and at least one supplied summer nighttime scene. Either node or multiple nodes may demonstrate the two states; this sentence does not require all six perspectives to appear. Text labels without reused scene imagery, or imagery inconsistent with the delivered views, fail.
